Description: Fragments of a Hebrew Psalms copy from Qumran Cave 4, in Hasmonean script. Its order differs from the Masoretic Psalter: Psalm 147 appears before Psalm 104, and a Psalm 106 passage has been debated as part of its sequence. Preserved-passage ranges for this manuscript are given in English (KJV) numbering; the manuscript itself carries no modern psalm numbers. Note on the Psalm 146 range: the 146:10 reading follows the Wikipedia-derived list; Ulrich's Index and DJD XVI give Psalm 106:48 for this material instead — the identification is left as 146:10 pending resolution.
Significance: An early Hebrew witness to the Psalms, predating the medieval Masoretic manuscripts by about a thousand years. Its chief value is textual: it shows which psalms and which readings were already in circulation in the Second Temple period, and, where its psalm order differs from the Masoretic Psalter, that the order of the Psalter was not yet fully fixed.
